findings.summary: The coverage record claims all eighteen acceptance checks pass today, but on this exact tree — with this round's assertion in it, no other change, and the file restored byte-identical — `bun test` exits 1 with acceptance 16's announced case failing, so rows 1 and 16 record as passing a criterion whose proof is not reproducible.
findings.evidence: Rows 1 and 16 are `red: false`. Row 1's reason: "`bun test` from the root is 884 pass, 0 fail, exit 0". Row 16's reason: "the two tests write the real page to disk and run the real bundle entry over it in a real DOM, one process per case, and both pass in the run above (1289.89ms and 1102.57ms)". Live counterexample, run from /Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/.claude/worktrees/kit-walkthrough-targets with `make build && make test` running concurrently and no file changed (git status = one modified file, HEAD eaa0224): BUN_UNDER_LOAD_EXIT=1, `(fail) what a drawn page says about being narrated > a page the helper announced itself on says nothing about not being narrated [3294.62ms]`, `error: expect(received).toEqual(expected)` with Received `["This page cannot be narrated here: JARVIS serves the story helper that rings a beat and points at what the beat is about, and nothing answered for it at this page's origin."]` at /Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/.claude/worktrees/kit-walkthrough-targets/ts/metalang/render.test.ts:468. It is a plain assertion failure at 3.3s, not the 5s timeout the earlier Prove-It round fixed (READING_A_PAGE = 60_000 at render.test.ts). The mechanism is in the test surface itself: /Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/.claude/worktrees/kit-walkthrough-targets/ts/metalang/client.tsx:65 registers `document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', read, { once: true })` during the harness's `await import(entry)`, while the harness sets `dom.window.__jarvisStory = true` only AFTER its wait-for-first-render loop, on the written claim that this is "the order a browser puts them in" (HARNESS comment, render.test.ts). jsdom fires its OWN DOMContentLoaded independently of the harness's manual dispatch — proved directly with the repo's pinned jsdom 31.0.0: a listener registered immediately after `new JSDOM(...)` fired on its own within a 50ms await, readyState `complete` (probe at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-timothystockstill-code-macos-4thWAIV-agent-guard/35473c11-0419-4893-8f1d-297a9a2adba7/scratchpad/probe.mjs). So when that natural event lands before the announcement is written, the announced case reads no helper and draws the line, and acceptance 16 ("a page where the helper announced itself shows none") and acceptance 1 ("`bun test` green") go red with correct production code. Required evidence that remains unproven: acceptance 1 and 16 green reproducibly rather than on one run. Five solo `bun test` runs on this tree were 884 pass / 0 fail exit 0, and `make build && make test` was 834 passed exit 0, which is why this is a reproducibility defect in the recorded proof and not a disagreement about the numbers.

observations.evidence: ts/metalang/check.ts:1004-1005 is `if (already !== undefined) fail(`${where}.id`, `"${id}" is already the id of ${already}`)`, first committed in fc5fa76 (2026-10-19), before this contract; ts/metalang/check.test.ts:216 already pins that wording. The page draws it as `problem | declare[1].constant.id | "IGuard" is already the id of declare[0].constant` beside both declarations' own sections, so the clash is reported and nothing resolves to the first. The direction told the author to rule and say so in the notes rather than bend the assertion, and it did.
